title: How to use Wallet passes for BFCM referral offers
summary: A practical guide to making Black Friday and Cyber Monday referral offers easier to save, find, share, and use with Wallet passes.
body_markdown:
BFCM offers do not need more email. They need a place customers can save, reopen, and act on when the sale is live.


A practical BFCM field guide


Black Friday and Cyber Monday turn every inbox into a traffic jam. A referral offer can still be useful, but only if a customer can find it when they are ready to shop or share. A Wallet pass gives the offer a small, durable home on the phone.


This is not a case for more notifications. It is a case for a more useful campaign asset. A saved pass gives the offer another route back to the customer when the sale is live. The job for a referral team is simple: make the offer easier to keep, then update it only when the customer has a real reason to act.


A good BFCM Wallet pass feels kept, not chased. It tells a customer what they have, what changed, and what to do next.


From the Talkable Wallet BFCM field guide.


## Give the offer a job at each point in the sale


A pass should change with the customer’s actual situation. Before the event, the job is to earn the save. During the event, it is to make the current offer easy to find. After a successful referral, it is to bring an earned reward back when it can still be used.


01 / SAVE IT


### Put real value on the pass


Early access, a live friend offer, or a referral reward with a clear end date gives someone a reason to keep it.


02 / FIND IT AGAIN


### Make the live offer obvious


Lead with the current reward or friend offer. The pass should answer the question in seconds.


03 / SEND IT


### Make sharing timely


Prompt customers who saved but have not shared when the live sale makes that action useful.


04 / USE IT


### Bring back earned value


Remind customers about active rewards near a real deadline. If nothing is available, do not manufacture urgency.


Meet customers in the moments that matter. From the Talkable Wallet BFCM field guide.


## Write updates around a real change


A pass should reflect the customer’s real situation. That is a useful operating rule for BFCM. A pass update should explain something that actually changed: the sale is live, the friend offer is active, or an earned reward is about to expire.


> “Your BFCM referral offer is saved. Share it with a friend and keep your reward ready for the sale.”


That works after a save because it confirms the offer is there and names the next sensible action. When Black Friday goes live, the message can become more direct: “Black Friday is on. Open Wallet to see your referral offer and reward.”


Moment What the pass should say What the customer can do


After save The offer is stored and the expiry is clear. Keep it, then share it.


Black Friday launch The current friend offer and reward are live. Open the pass and send the referral.


Final hours An earned reward still has usable value. Redeem before the real deadline.


> “Black Friday is on. Open Wallet to see your referral offer and reward.”


Plan for the pass itself to carry the value. A reminder can bring someone back, but the pass should still make sense when they open it later.


## Build a campaign asset, not a tiny website


The pass has a small amount of attention to work with. Put the reward or friend offer first. Make BFCM visible. Keep sharing and referral information close to the offer. Avoid trying to recreate a full landing page in a card-sized space.


VALUE FIRST


### No decoding required


Use a clear offer, a clear reward, and a real end date. Customers should not need to hunt through a terms page to know what is live.


EVENT-SPECIFIC


### Let it look like BFCM


Use sale-specific language and creative, but keep the treatment readable and recognizably part of the brand.


ACTION CLOSE


### Keep sharing within reach


Referral information and useful links belong next to the offer, not several screens away.


STATUS HONEST


### Show the real state


Do not call a reward earned until program rules have actually marked it eligible.


From the Talkable Wallet BFCM field guide.


## Plan around the sale calendar


Run the Wallet plan on the same clock as the promotion. That keeps each update attached to a reason instead of turning the pass into another automated message stream.


Before BFCM


### Earn the save


Introduce Wallet as a place to keep early access or a live referral offer before the event begins.


Black Friday


### Make the offer unmistakable


Update the pass so the current reward and customer action are clear at a glance.


Weekend


### Make sharing timely


Talk to saved-pass customers who have not shared. The live sale is the reason to act.


Last call


### Make reward use easy


Bring active, unused rewards back before the deadline. Leave customers alone if there is no value left.


> “Your reward is still in Wallet. Use it before the offer expires.”


From the Talkable Wallet BFCM field guide.


## Measure the next action, not just the install


An install is the beginning. The better signal is whether the saved offer moves someone to participate or use an earned reward. Watch the sequence, and use it to improve the next update.


Wallet BFCM scorecard


**Install rate** Are customers saving the offer?


**First referral share** Does the saved pass prompt participation?


**Reward redemption** Are earned rewards used before expiry?


**Wallet-attributed sales** Is Wallet contributing to the sale?


Do not declare victory because a pass was installed. If the offer is easier to keep and easier to use, the behavior will show up in the steps that follow.


## BFCM Wallet pre-launch checklist


- ✓


Confirm the friend offer, advocate reward, and expiry date are accurate.


- ✓


Make the live offer and next action readable in a quick glance.


- ✓


Map each pass update to a real sale moment and remove generic reminders.


- ✓


Test the referral link, reward status, and expiry handling on a real device.


- ✓


Decide which four signals will show whether the pass changed campaign behavior.


Wallet works best as a practical extension of a referral campaign. Give customers an offer worth keeping. Make it easy to reopen when the sale is live. Then let actual value, not a noisy cadence, decide when the pass speaks again.


## Frequently asked questions


What should a BFCM referral Wallet pass show first?


Lead with the customer’s active friend offer or reward, followed by a clear expiry and the next action. The customer should not have to decode the offer.


When should we ask customers to save the pass?


Before BFCM begins, when the pass holds early access, an active referral offer, or another useful benefit with a real end date.


How often should a Wallet pass be updated during BFCM?


Only when the customer’s situation changes. Good reasons include the sale going live, a timely sharing moment, or a genuinely usable reward approaching expiry.


Can a pass show that a referral reward is earned?


It can show the customer-facing status provided by the referral and commerce systems. The pass should not imply a reward is earned before program rules have validated it.


Should Wallet replace BFCM email?


No. Wallet gives a saved offer another way back to the customer. Email, site messaging, and paid channels still have their own jobs in the campaign.


Which metrics matter after an install?


Track first referral share, reward redemption, and Wallet-attributed sales alongside install rate. Those behaviors show whether the saved pass helped move the campaign forward.
